chapter: Radio, theaters and early dance forms
title: Band sizes in the twenties, Ted Demuth and theater orchestras
summary: DeDroit describes his seven- or eight-piece bands, trombonist Ted Demuth in his Marine uniform, and theater orchestras with big sax sections.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: But how many members were in your band in the twenties?

In the twenties. Now let me explain to you. I would give them anything they wanted. I had big bands. I'd picture here, show you, oh, old Star outfits. I had seven key men. Two trumpets, three saxes, and three rhythms. And I used to use them. For a while I used Ted Demuth, he's the leader here, isn't he? Ted. Yeah. Yeah. A fine trombone player. And Ted was in the Marines at that time. He used to come on a boat in his Marine uniform to play the first set, because he just so much could make it. And I wasn't going to stop the guy from making dollars, making drills, you know. Ted didn't have it so sweet, you know, in the beginning. I don't know what he was doing now, but he's a darling fellow. He's one of the nicest people I ever, he used to come late so often on his yard. The fellows used to call him the late Mr. Demuth. But he didn't, he was a good guy. He's my friend of the Union now, you know. He played with the Oriental Man the last concert, didn't he? Yeah. See, you know, they said, they do well. I don't know where they carried me back. And did you kill me when you put my pitch up there on the last, the last? Oh, I said, now who did that? I didn't know anything about it, you know.
Do you remember orchestras that were back in those days that sounded like the New Leviathan Orchestra does?

Well, I would say that most of the theater orchestras sounded like it. They weren't as big as that, you know what I mean? No. Because they start putting like Lowestate and the Palace, they put a ton of sax in a pit. Alvin Galladora played alto sax at the office. You read Alvin Galladora? I know him, yeah. He's one of the greatest. You know him? Yeah, sure. He's great. He's great.
